appraisal_events.evidence: « ... vous verrez pourquoi je vous choisis pour confident. Et puis aussi, pour une autre raison que vous saurez un jour. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann singles out the narrator as the sole person to whom he will recount his significant private conversation with the Prince de Guermantes, explicitly marking him as specially trusted.

status_effects.explanation: Being chosen by Swann as his exclusive confidant for a weighty, private account momentarily elevates the narrator's standing as a trusted interlocutor within the scene.

ambiguities: Charlus's praise of the unnamed portrait painter and his glancing jab at Mme de Saint-Euverte's taste ('un chef-d'oeuvre ait si mauvais goût') were considered but judged too marginal/witticism-driven to constitute material local positioning of 'le peintre' or 'marquise de Saint-Euverte'; a stricter reading could score one or both.
